notes.general_comments:
With all these multiple choice papers, there is considerable time pressure on candidates to complete the
questions within the time limit of an hour. This makes it necessary for candidates to have all the basic facts
of the subject at instant recall. It also means that there is little time available for double checking. Checking
of answers needs to be built in as part of the initial process. As the question is read, key facts should be
written. Space is available on the paper for working and it helps to avoid careless mistakes if, for example,
the power of a lamp given as 24 W is written “power = 24 J s–1”. Powers of ten are a source of many errors
with numerical questions. These arise not just by putting numbers into a calculator wrongly but also with the
metric system prefixes, mega, kilo, milli etc.
The mean mark was 23.4 and the standard deviation was 7.4. 13 candidates scored full marks, a
remarkable achievement for those candidates. Only a few of the questions showed low discrimination and
most of these were the easy questions, deliberately included to lessen the time pressure. Overall there was
good discrimination for the test.
9702 Physics June 2010
